scored.label: GPT-4.1 Mini
scored.note: The only clean answer to the fourth question: 'The failure of the argument does not imply that no fair allocation rule exists; it only shows the argument does not validly prove that conclusion' — stated and not reversed. Its countermodel names a list and two criteria but its rule is circular ('prioritising A when Criterion 1 is decisive') and it never checks that the rule ignores no criterion, so the verification point is withheld.

scored.label: Gemini 3.7 Flash
scored.note: Complete and concrete: a two-patient additive-score countermodel with an explicit sensitivity check, and it named the fallacy fallacy by name. Credit for that criterion is withheld because it then undercut it — 'providing a functional, aggregate-benefit-maximizing rule ... positively shows that fair allocation rules can exist', and its conclusion field asserts fair rules 'are indeed possible'. Premise 3 is a necessary condition only. This is the same stated-then-reversed pattern for which credit was withheld from GPT-5 Mini in the exploratory run, adjudicated identically here.
